Is object Y on screen? Loads its sprite slot into X (0 when it has none) and returns carry set when it has one and its era and room are the current ones. 40 callers: the puzzles test their objects with it.

The gnome lets go of what he carries: the slot is told to ignore its collision with the gnome until they part ($1A,x), the object's era and room become the current ones, and its x is kept (one of 200 or more is pulled back to 1) and its y set 21 lines below the gnome's top less one line for every 3 bytes of its sprite, so its bottom rests at the gnome's feet. Dropping object $2A also moves object $29, when it has a sprite, to sit 21 lines above it, and records $29's era and room. 12 callers.

Do the sprites in slots X and Y overlap? Builds a box at sprite Y's position, moved back by the width and height of sprite X's object and as wide and tall as both objects together (widths from obj_width, heights from obj_height), and tests sprite X's position against it (box_test). Carry set when they overlap. Keeps X and Y. 43 callers.

Is the point ($06, $07) inside the trapezoid at trapezoid_table + X? The four bytes are a top row, a bottom row, and the left and right x at the top; each edge moves one step outward for every two rows down, as the floor of a room drawn in perspective does. Lets the gnome's step through only where a list of rectangles at ($0F) allows it: five bytes each, x, width, y, height and a flag, ended by $FF. Gives object Y a sprite: takes the highest free slot from 7 down (none free returns with N set and X = $FF), and for a world object (4 or more) records the slot in obj_slot and takes the object's x and y. Then falls into sprite_object. 69 callers: 66 jsr and 3 jmp.

Shows object Y in slot X: sets the sprite's colour, multicolour and x-expansion from obj_flags, clears 63 bytes of its buffer and its move, sets its frame to $FF and its animation delay to 1 so that the next sprite_update steps to frame 0 and draws it, and switches it on. Moves and animates slot X. When its animation delay ($63,x) runs out it steps to the next frame, wrapping after the frame count from obj_anim and reloading the delay from the same byte; on a new frame it copies the frame (sprite_draw). Every pass it adds the slot's move ($53,x, $5B,x) to its x and y, writes the sprite's position (sprite_set_x, sprite_set_y) and clears the move. 41 callers.

Copies frame $6B,x of the slot's object into the slot's sprite buffer: the frame's address is obj_gfx_lo/hi plus the frame number times the frame's size (obj_size); the bytes go in rows of 1, 2 or 3 (obj_flags bits 4-5) and the rest of each 3-byte row is skipped. Points $11-$12 at slot X's sprite buffer, $EC00 + 64 x X. Two callers.

Eight bytes, $01, $02, $04 ... $80: the bit of each sprite slot.

Command $B: steps back to the command before and runs it again at once. After command $A it makes a loop that warbles every pass until the effect is stopped.
Command $A: loads $80 and runs on into sfx_cmd_warble.

Command 9 (and $A): one step of a warble. It subtracts the frequency's low byte from itself (sbc $86,x), so the $40 or $80 loaded first is overwritten and never used: the low byte becomes $FF and the high byte drops by one. From that high byte, h, it plays a high byte of 255 - h - 6 (less 8 more when h is odd) and a low byte of 7, so the pitch climbs as h falls, with a wobble. Then it waits one pass.
Commands 7 and 8: back to the effect's first command ($84), run at once.
Command 6: the frequency's high byte up by one, then as sfx_cmd_slide_down.

Command 5: the frequency's high byte down by one. The argument is a count: the first time it is loaded into $7E, and the command repeats every two passes until the count has run out, A + 1 steps in all; then the script moves on.
Command 4: moves on and waits A passes, writing the voice's registers.
Command 3: the sustain level ($82) drops by one; until it reaches 0 the command repeats every A passes, and then the script moves on at once.

Command 2: waveform and sustain from sfx_waves entry A: the low nibble is the sustain level ($82), the high nibble the waveform, kept with the gate bit set ($8A). The gate is closed first, so the envelope starts again. Then the next command at once.
Command 1: the frequency ($86, $88) from entry A of sfx_pitch_lo and sfx_pitch_hi, then the next command at once.
Moves to the next command and runs it.
Command 0: the effect ends: position and sustain 0, the gate closed, the registers written.
Writes the channel's voice: frequency ($D400-$D401), sustain level ($D406, release 0) and control ($D404). Then the next channel.
The twelve sound-effect commands' addresses, by the high nibble of the script byte: 0 end, 1 pitch, 2 waveform, 3 fade, 4 wait, 5 slide down, 6 slide up, 7 and 8 loop, 9 and $A warble, $B again.
The handler addresses' high bytes, read here by sfx_command, one byte after their low bytes.
Waveforms and sustain levels for command 2, the waveform in the high nibble ($1x triangle, $2x sawtooth, $8x noise) and the sustain level in the low nibble.
Low bytes of the six frequencies for command 1: $2187, $323C, $13EF, $080C, $D0C3 and $F0FF.
High bytes of the frequencies for command 1.

Where each of the seven sound effects starts in sfx_script (position 0 means no effect). 0: noise fading every 3 passes; 1: noise sliding down 12 steps; 2: noise sliding up in a loop; 3: the time trip's rising warble, eight steps and again; 4: a warble every pass until stopped (the teleport); 5: low noise fading every 4 passes; 6: a burst of noise every 16 passes, until stopped.

Stops the music: the tempo mask $A0 is zeroed, then into sid_clear. Six callers.
Zeroes every SID register and sets the volume to 15. Called when the game is paused and by music_stop.

Starts tune X / 4 (X = 0, 4, ... $1C): stops the music and clears the SID, zeroes both voices' state ($96-$9B) with a length of 1, so the first step fetches a note, and copies the tune's four bytes from tune_table to $9C-$9F. The caller then sets the tempo mask $A0, which starts it. Three callers: era_enter, and play_state for the flute.
The eight tunes, four bytes each: the low bytes of the first and second voice's data, then their high bytes.

The music, once a frame from the raster interrupt. A step plays when the tempo mask $A0, the frame count $24 (counted here) and the pause flag $AF share a bit: era records' masks 1, 3, 7 and $FF make the music play on half, three quarters, seven eighths or all but one in 256 of the frames. $A1 counts the steps from 3 down to 0. Each voice (X = 1 on SID voice 2, X = 0 on SID voice 3) counts its note's length ($96,x) down; when it is not over, every fourth step (when $A1 is 0) its sustain ($98,x) drops a level, so each note fades.

The voice's next pair from its data ($9C,x and $9E,x; index $9A,x moves on by 2 first): a note byte with bit 7 set sends the voice back to its first pair. The note sets sustain 7 ($D406 = $70, also $98,x = 7), the frequency from note_lo and note_hi, and the triangle waveform with its gate opened again ($10, then $11); the length goes to $96,x.
The next voice, SID voice 3 ($0E).
Low bytes of the music's 60 frequencies, by note number. Note 0 is 0, a rest; notes 1-53 fall a semitone at a time from $547D; notes 54-59 are higher again, from $5983 to $861E.
High bytes of the music's frequencies, by note number.
